## Intent
Hypothesis: a branchless blend walk with per-particle hash RNG eliminates per-particle branch divergence and can approach the streaming ceiling on death-free workloads.

## Cache saturation
All measured N (4000–4M) exceed the L1d spill at N≈963, so the L1d→L2 transition is not visible. From N=4000 to N=16000 cost falls sharply at every death rate (10.33→6.07 ns/p at q=0.01; 11.32→8.23 at q=0.25), reflecting fixed overhead amortization. Past N=16000 the curve is flat through the L2 spill at N≈61680 with no knee: at q=0.01 it goes 6.07→5.90→5.86 ns/p across N=16000/65000/262000. At the largest N (1M–4M) a slight rise appears (6.02→6.15 at q=0.01), suggesting TLB or DRAM latency creeping in. Death rate raises the floor — from ~5.9 to ~6.3 to ~8.4 ns/p at large N — without altering the N-shape, confirming the blend loop itself is branch-tolerant and the extra cost is uniform per particle.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 11.6 GB/s at N=262000, q=0.01, which is 46% of the 25.22 GB/s streaming ceiling. The cell is overhead-bound at small N (6.58 GB/s at N=4000) and stabilizes at ~11.5 GB/s for N≥16000, never approaching the ceiling. Death rate degrades the plateau: 11.6→10.8→8.04 GB/s as q rises from 0.01 to 0.05 to 0.25, a 31% loss at q=0.25. The bandwidth never transitions to streaming-bound; it plateaus well below ceiling regardless of N, indicating a compute or scatter-latency bottleneck rather than DRAM throughput.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized across the four components of a single particle, not across particles: `ldur q18` loads 16 bytes (4 floats), `ext.16b v20, v18, v19, #0xc` rearranges components, and `fmul.4s`/`fadd.4s` process all four lanes at once. A gather appears as `ld1.s {v19}[1], [x22]`, inserting one scalar into a vector lane. The walk2 scatter is entirely scalar: 17 `strb` instructions perform byte-granular stores, each preceded by `ldrb`/`add`/`cmp`/`csel` saturation clamps. These per-byte scalar stores — not the vectorized blend — cap bandwidth at 46% of ceiling, since the scatter cannot stream contiguous cache lines.

## Verdict
Partially — the branchless blend shows no cache-spill knee and flat scaling past N=16000 (5.86 ns/p at q=0.01, N=262000), confirming branch-tolerance in the walk1 loop. But the cell never exceeds 11.6 GB/s = 46% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling because the walk2 scatter's 17 `strb` byte stores cannot stream, and death rate degrades the plateau to 8.04 GB/s at q=0.25. The hypothesis holds for the blend walk's cache behavior but is refuted on the streaming-ceiling claim.
